name: KHAN YOU DIG IT?
clue: His burial site was kept so secret it remains unfound; the empire this steppe conqueror founded became history's largest contiguous one

name: INITIAL HERE
clue: A congressman's error on his West Point paperwork gave this Ohio-born Union commander & future president the apt initials 'U.S.'

name: A PLACE IN THE NAME
clue: Born in 1820 while her wealthy English parents were touring Italy, the founder of modern nursing was named for her birth city

name: CROSS PURPOSES
clue: Honoring founder Henry Dunant's homeland, the Red Cross flag reverses the colors of this country's square banner

name: ROCK OF AGES
clue: Its smaller bluestones were hauled some 150 miles from Wales to Salisbury Plain; its main axis lines up with the solstice sun

name: DEMOTION COMMOTION
clue: An 11-year-old English schoolgirl named this world discovered in 1930; its 2-letter symbol also honors Percival Lowell

name: CHAIN REACTIONS
clue: After 1945's Trinity test, this Manhattan Project lab director recalled the Bhagavad Gita: 'Now I am become Death'

name: FOILED AGAIN!
clue: Once so costly it was displayed beside France's crown jewels, this lightweight metal crowned the Washington Monument in 1884

name: SUE-PERSTAR
clue: Named for the fossil hunter who spotted her in South Dakota in 1990, Sue is the Field Museum's $8.36 million specimen of this species

name: COVER STORIES
clue: Born in British India, Eric Blair served as a colonial policeman in Burma before warning of Big Brother under this pen name

name: MEMORY LANE
clue: Andrew Lloyd Webber set T.S. Eliot's playful 1939 verse collection to music in this show, once Broadway's longest-running

name: POETRY IN MOTION
clue: Baltimore's NFL team takes its name from an 1845 poem by this writer, who died in that city & was buried there in 1849

name: WAR PAINT
clue: At his request, this Spaniard's stark mural of a 1937 town bombing stayed at New York's MoMA until democracy returned to Spain

name: SWAN SONGS
clue: Dead at 35 in 1791, this Salzburg-born prodigy left his Requiem unfinished; his pupil Süssmayr completed the mass

name: FOLK HEROES
clue: The 2016 Nobel in Literature went to this Minnesota-born songwriter for 'new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition'

name: QUIET ON THE SET
clue: This silent-film icon co-founded United Artists in 1919; his 1972 honorary Oscar drew a 12-minute standing ovation

name: MR. NICE GUY
clue: This ordained Presbyterian minister won over a skeptical 1969 Senate panel, and $20 million for public TV, by reciting a gentle lyric

name: HOME COURT ADVANTAGE
clue: The Flushing Meadows home of tennis's US Open is named for this champion, who won 1973's 'Battle of the Sexes'

name: SIEGE THE DAY
clue: Homer's Iliad never mentions it; Virgil's Aeneid holds the most famous ancient account of this hollow ruse that ended a 10-year war

name: BORN AGAIN & AGAIN
clue: Tibetan Buddhists hold that each bearer of this title is the rebirth of the one before; the 14th won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize

name: CRUMBS OF WISDOM
clue: A fixture of American Chinese restaurants, this folded dessert likely began with Japanese bakers & is scarcely found in China

name: SHORT & SWEET
clue: This 2-letter word began as a jokey 1839 Boston abbreviation of 'oll korrect'; clubs backing 'Old Kinderhook' Van Buren spread it

name: BARRIER TO ENTRY
clue: Manhattan's famed finance lane takes its name from a wooden palisade the Dutch erected in the 1650s to guard New Amsterdam

name: CORPS VALUES
clue: Sent by Jefferson to explore his vast new purchase, this pair & their Corps of Discovery reached the Pacific in 1805
